title: Investigation of intrusive emotional internal images with reference to neurobiological bases of emotion processing - a translational study in patients with social anxiety disorder
summary:
Social anxiety disorder is one of the most debilitating mental disorders. The main characteristic is the pronounced and persistent fear in social situations, which leads to avoidance or endurance of these under extreme stress. Despite evidence-based treatment options, these are unsuccessful in up to 50% of patients. There is a lack of linkage between basic neurobiological processes and specific symptoms and the development of targeted interventions.
Emotion processing is a crucial mechanism for mental health, but neuroscientific findings have hardly been linked to the symptoms of social anxiety and are therefore insufficient for the development of optimized treatments. Intrusive social imagery, a key process in the maintenance of social anxiety disorder, may be a promising target for neurobiologically based treatment approaches. These images are often visual and intrude unexpectedly and involuntarily into the sufferer's thoughts, are very unpleasant and contribute to the maintenance of social anxiety disorder.
One approach to reducing these images focuses on the interruption of the memory storage process by a competing task. To date, there are no neuroscientific findings on the neurobiological correlates of these images in social anxiety disorder and their treatment. Also, cognitive interference tasks to reduce the frequency of these images have not yet been applied.
In this study, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) will be used to investigate the neurobiological basis of intrusive social images in social anxiety disorder. In addition, the modifiability of these images will be tested using a competing interference task and the feasibility of an intervention focused on this will be investigated. The results could both improve our understanding of the development and maintenance of social anxiety disorder and contribute to the further development of specific psychotherapeutic treatment methods.

interventions.name: Participants who meet the diagnostic criteria for social anxiety disorder, can report at least one intrusive social image and will be given a visual-spatial interference task (bringing the intrusive social image into mind, playing tetris with mental rotation for at least 20 minutes) to reduce intrus

Participants who meet the diagnostic criteria for social anxiety disorder, can report at least one intrusive social image and are given an auditory interference task (i.e. attentive listing to a podcast for at least 20 minutes) to reduce intrusive emotional images (control condition)
Healthy controls who do not meet diagnostic criteria for mental illness (acute or lifetime) and can report at least one intrusive social image

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Report of at least one intrusive emotional images with social reference.

HC: individuals without any psychiatric disorder current or lifetime
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria: For healthy control, any current or life-time psychiatric disorder is an exclusion criterion.
Further exclusion criteria for all subjects: Centrally acting medication, neurological abnormalities, organically induced mental illness, dementia, CNS injuries, MRI contraindications, left-handedness.
